To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a database of RNA secondary structures for 86 000 sequences and that the database is available at http://its2.
we developed an algorithm that allows the prediction of the ITS2 structure and implemented it in a database.
The ITS2 Database is a comprehensive resource for all ITS2 sequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the evolution of the ITS2 structure and the development of the ITS2 as a phylogenetic marker.
the development of a new approach to predict RNA structures and to use the structure of the highly conserved ITS2 region for molecular systematics.
understanding the structural variability of the ITS2 and the effects of structural differences in terms of phylogenetic information content.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ITS2 structure is highly conserved, but that the homologous structure is only relative to the standard structure.
the ITS2 is a highly promising tool for molecular systematics and that homology models are a useful tool for the prediction of the structure of the ITS2.
the ITS2 has the potential to be a standard marker for molecular systematic studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ITS2 structure is the most conserved part of the ITS2 sequence.
the ITS2 is the best candidate to predict the structure by homology modelling.
the ITS2 is a suitable marker for higher level analyses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is an important group of organisms with a unique ITS2 structure that has not been described yet and is not covered in the database.
a wide range of species can be classified by the ITS2 structure.
the ITS2 is not only highly conserved in sequence but also in structure.
